title: Marcus added a token check to the payout endpoint
brief: After the breach, Marcus has patched the payout endpoint himself and wants it merged tonight. It looks like the fix you wrote earlier. Read it as if the attacker were reading it too.

reasons.text: A request that leaves the token out skips the check entirely.
!== is not a constant-time comparison, so the token can be guessed by timing.
It should also check the Referer header.
The token belongs in a header, not the request body.

reasonExplanations.timing: a fair point for secrets checked millions of times, but irrelevant here: the attacker does not need to guess the token when leaving it out works
reasonExplanations.referer: Referer can be absent for legitimate users; adding it would not fix the hole that is already there
reasonExplanations.header: either place works, since another site's form cannot read the token in the first place
reasonExplanations.missing: this patch is not correct -- a forged form simply omits csrfToken

attackSuite.payload: A forged form with no csrfToken field at all
attackSuite.label: Walks straight past the check

functionalSuite.value: The account page's own form, carrying its token
functionalSuite.label: Still accepted

hints: Trace the if statement when csrfToken is undefined. Which branch runs?
A check that only runs when the attacker volunteers the evidence is not a check.
